dublinCore.description: The short-time Fourier transform of a chirp, a frequency-shift-keyed signal or a note sequence is computed with a radix-2 FFT and drawn as a spectrogram, with a waveform, a time cursor and the spectrum of the frame at the cursor. Sliders for window length and overlap show the trade-off between time resolution and frequency resolution.
relation: Chapter 7: DFT, FFT and Frequency Domain Analysis

topic: Window length, overlap and hop size
learningObjectives: Explain why a spectrogram is needed for a signal whose frequency content changes with time
Compute the time span, bin spacing and hop size of an STFT from the window length, sampling rate and overlap
Analyze how the window length trades time resolution against frequency resolution
Choose STFT settings that suit a given signal
prerequisites: The DFT, bin spacing and window functions

misconceptions.misconception: A longer window always gives a better spectrogram
misconceptions.correction: A longer window narrows the bins but blurs changes in time; the product of time span and bin spacing is always 1
misconceptions.evidence: With the chirp, the ridge is about twice as thick at N = 1024 as at N = 256, and the FSK bit edges are blurred over about 128 ms

misconceptions.misconception: Increasing the overlap improves the resolution
misconceptions.correction: Overlap only sets the hop size and the number of frames; resolution is fixed by the window length and the window type
misconceptions.evidence: Change the Overlap slider from 0% to 90% at N = 256: the hop falls from 256 to 26 samples but the ridge keeps its thickness

accessibility.screenReaderScript: A waveform with a movable time cursor, a spectrogram with time across and frequency upward, and beside it the spectrum of the frame at the cursor. Menus choose the signal, window, colour map and scale, and sliders set the window length and the overlap of the short-time Fourier transform.

controls.label: Signal
controls.description: Chooses the test signal: a linear chirp, a frequency-shift-keyed bit stream or a sequence of notes

options.label: Note sequence (C5 E5 G5 C6 G5)

controls.label: Window
controls.description: Chooses the window function applied to each frame before the FFT

controls.label: Window length N
controls.description: Steps the window length through 32, 64, 128, 256, 512 and 1024 samples (the slider position 0 to 5 selects the entry); the banner shows the time span and bin spacing

controls.label: Overlap (%)
controls.description: Sets the overlap between successive frames, which sets the hop size H = N(1 - overlap) and the number of frames

controls.label: Colour map
controls.description: Chooses the colour map used for the spectrogram and the colour bar

controls.label: Scale
controls.description: Chooses how the magnitude is mapped to colour: decibels over an 80 dB range, linear magnitude or linear power

visualElements.description: Waveform of the signal with the N samples of the selected frame shaded and a red time cursor
Spectrogram: time across, frequency upward, colour for level; each rectangle is one STFT value
Spectrum of the frame at the cursor, drawn sideways on the frequency axis of the spectrogram, with a dashed line at the true signal frequency and a colour bar
Banner with the time span, bin spacing and their product, and a box with the cursor time, frame number and hop size

model.description: Radix-2 FFT of windowed frames of a synthesized one-second signal sampled at 8000 Hz
equations: X[m, k] = sum over n of x[n + m H] w[n] e^(-j 2 pi k n / N)
time span of the window = N / fs, bin spacing = fs / N, product = 1
hop H = N (1 - overlap), frames = floor((Ns - N) / H) + 1
algorithms: Hann, Hamming, Blackman and rectangular windows in DFT-periodic form
assumptions: fs = 8000 Hz and the signal is 8000 samples (1 s) long
The FFT length equals the window length (no zero-padding), so each bin is drawn as one cell
Each frame is plotted at the centre of its N samples; times where no complete window fits are left blank
Levels are scaled so that a steady bin-centred sinusoid of amplitude 1 reads 0 dB; the dB scale spans 80 dB
All three signals are synthesized; no recorded speech or music is used

instructionalStrategies: Change one STFT parameter at a time and relate the shape of the time-frequency cells to the computed resolutions
Predict-then-verify with the window length slider and the pointer readout
extensions: Add a two-tone signal to measure the smallest resolvable frequency spacing
Zero-pad each frame to interpolate the spectrum
